pages.text: Dad repaired a net in the yard. Beside him was a basket of shells with holes in them.
They wanted to make a shell necklace and put it around Dad's neck. "Let us choose only shells with holes and thread them."
Lolo picked up thread and started adding shells. Riri laid out the shells and examined them. "Just start threading." "Choose matching pairs first."
Lolo threaded lots of shells. The thin thread pulled tight.
Snap! The thread broke, and shells scattered across the wooden floor.
Riri arranged shells by size. Neither this pair nor that pair was right.
The floor was covered with shells. Riri's thread was still empty.
Dad tossed them some thread left from repairing the net. It was thin, tough net thread.
Riri handed over shells, and Lolo threaded them quickly. The necklace grew longer and longer.
It wrapped around Dad's neck three times. Whenever he turned his head, it rattled and clattered. Dad ate dinner wearing it.
